[P1] 心不住鸟的舒科特
[法] 薇·瓦克尔/文
[法] 夏洛特·阿美灵/图
党 蔷/译

学会专心
心不在焉的舒科特
[法] 瑞·瓦克尔 / 文
[法] 夏洛特·阿美灵 / 图
党 蕾 / 译
APOTHEC
浙江少年儿童出版社
有限公司

[P3] 宝宝情绪管理图画书
学会专心
心不在焉的舒科特
[法]颜·瓦克尔/文
[法]夏洛特·阿美灵/图
党馨/译
时代出版传媒股份有限公司
安徽教育出版社

[P4] 出版者的话
古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：“任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但若要适时适所、以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难了。”我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所，对适当对象恰如其分地表达情绪。
现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。
情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期，一个人在幼儿时期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心发展影响很长远。
当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露，就能生根、发芽。
这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为家长亲子共读时的参考。
让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧！

[P5] 老师对你说
当幻想遇上心不在焉
这是一个引人入胜、充满魔力的小故事，瞧瞧故事里都有什么：浑身
翠绿、戴着浅粉色眼镜的小毛毛虫，长满红叶子的魔法学校，顶着白点的
红色大蘑菇，硕大无比的癞蛤蟆，自由绽放的各色小野花……怎么样，丰
富多彩吧？
更可贵的是，作者深谙儿童心理特点，通过一系列有趣的事件，把我
们引入了一个迷人的童话世界，我们仿佛能看到字里行间跳跃着一个活泼
可爱的儿童形象。
小毛虫舒科特看着天上的云朵，开始了幻想：一个女巫、一只大熊、
一只狼……幻想的后果是，舒科特和一只大苍蝇撞到了一起。负责管理交
通的雄蜂非常生气，责问她怎么这么心不在焉。到学校后，舒科特上课时
幻想，放学后又幻想，结果搞出了不少乱子，弄得大家都感叹她怎么这么
心不在焉。
第二天，舒科特决心不再做“白日梦”了！室外活动课有急事了，
舒科特的注意力十分集中，她一下子就成功啦！可是，一件恐怖的事情突
然发生了：一只可怕的癞蛤蟆要吃掉大家！舒科特临危不乱，认真念起魔
法口诀，迅速地把癞蛤蟆变小了。蜘蛛老师为她的机智勇敢鼓掌，舒科特

[P6] 自豪地表示，她再也不会心不在焉啦！
小毛毛虫舒科特，为什么让你感觉如此熟悉？你是那个偶尔会逃学的孩子，还是那个在课堂上会走神的孩子？其实，不必笑话舒科特，因为我们每个人都曾经是“小毛毛虫舒科特”。难道不是吗？贪玩、爱幻想就是孩子与生俱来的天性。
当然了，在日常学习和生活中，孩子需要一心一意，不能总是心不在焉。作为家长，我们要理解孩子，不要过分苛责，而要采取适当的方式方法，培养孩子的注意力和任务意识，让孩子明白幻想和注意力其实并不矛盾，要恰当地去幻想。
对家长而言，孩子就是一本值得细细阅读的“小人书”，他们有独特的精神世界，需要我们真诚地体会，耐心地倾听。只有这样，我们才能在顺应孩子天性的基础上，更好地引导孩子健康成长。
（全国百佳幼儿园园长 王立华）

[P7] 假期总算结束了，开学万岁！
小毛毛虫舒科特要去森林中央的老橡树洞魔法学校上学啦！

[P8] 小毛毛虫太高兴了，她把新书包塞得满满的，尽量什么东西都不落下。
“星星的粉末、几片玫瑰花瓣和一颗大蛇牙……我觉得东西都齐啦！”，

[P9] 哎呀！由于刚开学，去学校的路上实在是太拥挤了！
幸好，就像真正的小仙女一样，舒科特现在可以随意
变成蝴蝶了！

[P10] 她只要唱一下这首神奇的歌就可以了：
“哆来咪发唆，数到三，就起飞！一、二、三！”
“扑”的一声，舒科特真的变成会飞的小蝴蝶了！

[P11] 一阵微风吹来，看着天上的云朵，舒科特开始幻想了……

[P12] “这朵云看起来像个女巫，我还能看出来她鹰嘴似的鼻子和尖尖的帽子呢……啊！那朵云是灰色的，好像一只大熊！咦？他的鼻子变长啦……现在他好像是一只狼了……呀，好可怕！”

[P13] 因为在空中不停地胡思乱想，一不留神，舒科特就撞到了一只大苍蝇身上。
负责管理交通的雄蜂立刻吹着哨子赶了过来。
“我说，难道你今天上午不上课吗？”雄蜂怒吼道，“我的天呀，你怎么这么心不在焉！”

[P14] 舒科特有点羞愧，她加快速度，急匆匆地往学校所在的老橡树赶去。

[P15] 在走进教室之前，舒科特又变回了毛毛虫。她怯怯地敲了敲门。

[P16] “你迟到了，小姑娘！”蜘蛛老师不满地说，“坐在第一排这个树根上吧，把你的小坩埚拿出来。我们正在配制一种可以改变花朵颜色的药水……”

[P17] “照我这么做就行，”小萤火虫露西对舒科特小声说道，“得先用羊齿草的梗搅拌这些配料，当药水全都变成白色的时候，再加进去一小片彩虹……”

[P18] 小毛毛虫的眼镜上布满了水蒸气，她尝试着集中注意力……

[P19] 忽然，一束阳光透过窗户照了进来，笼罩在舒科特身上。
身上暖洋洋的，这种舒服的感觉让她回忆起了假期。

舒科特的嘴角洋溢着美美的微笑，她又开始幻想了……

[P20] “夏天的时候……我正在一片栗树叶上玩帆板呢……啧
啧，这可真美好呀……阳光抚摸着我的后背……可是……可是……可是……”

[P21] 可是，当舒科特还以为自己在湖面上的时候，她的药水开始翻腾起来，冒出好多大泡泡！
一个巨大的泡泡悄悄地形成了，从小坩埚里升了起来……
突然，“啪”的一声，那个泡泡爆炸了！
可怜的舒科特！她浑身上下都沾满了药水！

[P22] “你应该把火关小一点，”露西大笑道，“我的天呀，你怎么这么心不在焉啊！”,

[P23] 魔法学校
这一天总算要结束了！
经过了一天的各种波折，舒科特终于可以回家了！

[P24] 刚出校门，舒科特看到小瓢虫扎贝尔正在把蘑菇变成小刺猬呢！
“如果你愿意的话，”小瓢虫对舒科特说，“我可以教你一种神奇的魔法舞蹈，让你学会个好玩的把戏……”

[P25] 舒科特找了一朵大蘑菇当目标，这朵大蘑菇戴着一顶红帽子，这让她想起了……圣诞老人！
然后，她就又陷入了幻想中……

[P26] “亲爱的圣诞老人，今年我想要的礼物有：一罐金粉，用来装饰我的翅膀……一个鼻涕虫毛绒玩具，一些公主首饰，还有几块莴苣巧克力……”

[P27] 舒科特沉浸在对无数礼物的幻想中，她跳呀，跳呀，跳呀……完全忘记了周围的一切。
结果呢，这朵大蘑菇不仅没有变成小刺猬，还一直扭来扭去的，好像有人在给它挠痒痒似的。
然后呢，奇怪的事发生了：大蘑菇竟然长出了两条腿和两只大耳朵，“忽”的一下，它竟然蹦蹦跳跳地“逃跑”了……

[P28] “怎么会这样？！” 扎贝儿大声感叹道，她简直不敢相信自己的眼睛，“我的天呀，你怎么这么心不在焉啊！”

[P29] 第二天早晨，舒科特下定决心再也不做“白日梦”了！
而且，今天的室外活动课有意思极了，要学习如何把怪物变小。

[P30] 舒科特注意力十分集中，她对着一只旧鞋子进行练习，一下子就成功啦！
27

[P31] 突然，一件恐怖的事情发生了：一只可怕的黏糊糊的癫蛤蟆突然跳了出来！
“好美味呀！啧啧，有这么多可口的点心！”癫蛤蟆流着口水说道，“我应该先吃哪个好呢？”

[P32] 当大家都叫着逃跑的时候，癫蛤蟆慢慢地逼近了舒科特……

[P33] 幸好，舒科特这次已经认真地记住了魔法口诀。她急忙念道：
“凭借着大老鼠的法力，让这只恶心的大怪物迅速变成小东西吧！”

[P34] 就在这一秒钟的时间里，癫蛤蟆不断缩小，缩小，再缩小……
直到变得跟小飞虫一样大。

[P35] “干得漂亮，我的小姑娘！”蜘蛛老师鼓着掌说道，“如果没有你的话，我们可能都会变成癞蛤蟆肚子里的‘美餐’！”,

[P36] “不管怎么说，”舒科特自豪地说，“有一件事是肯定的：从今以后，我再也不会心不在焉啦！”

[P1] The Heart-Not-Still Bird Shuket
[France] Wei · Wacker / Text
[France] Charlotte Amelin / Illustrations
Dang Qiang / Translator

[P2] Children's Emotional Management Picture Book
Learn to Focus
Shuket, the Distracted One
[France] Rui Wacker / Text
[France] Charlotte Amelin / Illustrations
Dang Lei / Translator
APOTHEC
Zhejiang Children's Publishing House
Co., Ltd.

[P3] Children's Emotional Management Picture Book
Learn to Focus
The Distracted Shuket
[France] Yan Waker / Text
[France] Charlotte Amelin / Illustrations
Dang Xin / Translator
Times Publishing Media Co., Ltd.
Anhui Education Press

[P4] Publisher's Note
The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry, and that's not difficult. But to be angry at the right time, in the right place, with the right person, and in the right way—this is truly difficult.' What we now call emotional management means expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time and place, toward the right person.
In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills. Those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack it may be intelligent but often struggle in their endeavors.
While emotional management skills are partly influenced by innate factors, they ultimately depend on learning and development through experience. Early childhood is the golden period for cultivating emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits formed during this period create lasting neural connections in the brain, profoundly influencing a child's physical and mental development.
Currently, reading emotional management picture books together with children is a widely recognized method for developing these skills. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness. Through parents' voices, they enter children's ears, take root in their hearts, and with sunlight and rain, they grow and flourish.
This series of charming animal storybooks is warm and heartfelt. Each book focuses on a specific emotional topic for children, illustrating their inner journey and revealing how they overcome emotional challenges and solve problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, serving as a valuable reference for parents during shared reading.
Let us enjoy a wonderful journey of parent-child reading together with this series!

[P5] Teacher Says to You
When Imagination Meets Daydreaming
This is an engaging, magical little story. Look at what's in it: a green caterpillar wearing light pink glasses, a magic school covered in red leaves, a red mushroom with white spots, a huge toad, and colorful wildflowers blooming freely... How colorful and rich is that?
More valuable still, the author understands children's psychology well, and through a series of fun events, leads us into a charming fairy tale world. We can almost see a lively and lovely child figure leaping between the lines.
The little caterpillar Shuket looks at the clouds in the sky and begins to daydream: a witch, a big bear, a wolf... The result of her daydreaming is that Shuket bumps into a big fly. The male bee in charge of traffic is very angry and asks her why she is so absent-minded. At school, Shuket daydreams during class, and again after school, causing all sorts of messes, making everyone exclaim how absent-minded she is.
The next day, Shuket decides she won't daydream anymore! During the outdoor activity class, there's an urgent matter, and Shuket's attention is highly focused—she succeeds right away! But then, a terrifying thing suddenly happens: a scary toad is about to eat everyone! Shuket remains calm under pressure, recites the magic spell carefully, and quickly shrinks the toad. The spider teacher applauds her for her cleverness and bravery, and Shuket

[P6] Proudly declares, she will never be distracted again!
Little caterpillar Shuket, why does he feel so familiar to you? Are you the child who occasionally skips school, or the one who daydreams in class? Actually, don't laugh at Shuket, because we've all once been a 'little caterpillar Shuket'. Isn't that true? Being playful and imaginative is a natural trait of children.
Of course, in daily study and life, children need to focus and shouldn't always be distracted. As parents, we should understand our children, avoid being overly critical, and instead use appropriate methods to cultivate their attention and task awareness. We should help them understand that imagination and focus are not contradictory, and that imagination should be embraced appropriately.
To parents, children are like little books worth reading carefully. They have unique inner worlds that require our sincere understanding and patient listening. Only then can we guide them to grow up healthily while respecting their natural nature.
(National Top 100 Kindergarten Principal, Wang Lihua)

[P7] The vacation is finally over, hooray for school!
Little caterpillar Shuket is going to the Magic School in the old oak tree hollow in the middle of the forest!

[P8] The little caterpillar was so excited that she packed her new backpack full, trying not to leave anything behind.
"Stardust, a few rose petals, and a big snake tooth... I think I've got everything!"

[P9] Oh no! Since school just started, the way to school is so crowded!
Luckily, just like a real fairy, Shuket can now turn into a butterfly anytime!

[P10] She just needed to sing this magical song:
"Do-Re-Mi-Fa-So, count to three, and fly! One, two, three!"
"Puff" went the sound, and Shuket really turned into a flying little butterfly!

[P11] A gentle breeze blew, and looking at the clouds in the sky, Shuket began to daydream...

[P12] "This cloud looks like a witch, I can even see her eagle-like nose and pointy hat... Ah! That gray cloud looks like a big bear! Huh? His nose is getting longer... Now he looks like a wolf... Oh, how scary!"

[P13] Because she was daydreaming in the air, Shuket accidentally bumped into a big fly.
The male bee in charge of traffic immediately rushed over, blowing his whistle.
"Hey, aren't you supposed to be in class this morning?" the bee roared, "Goodness, how can you be so distracted!"

[P14] Shuket felt a bit ashamed, so she sped up and hurried toward the old oak tree where the school was located.

[P15] Before entering the classroom, Shuket turned back into a caterpillar. She timidly knocked on the door.

[P16] "You're late, little girl!" the spider teacher said impatiently. "Sit on this tree root in the front row, and take out your little crucible. We're currently brewing a potion that can change the color of flowers..."

[P17] "Just do it like this," the little firefly Lucy whispered to Shuket, "First, stir these ingredients with the stem of fern. When the potion turns completely white, add a tiny piece of rainbow..."

[P18] The little caterpillar's glasses were fogged up with steam, and she tried to focus her attention...

[P19] Suddenly, a beam of sunlight shone through the window and fell upon Shuket.
Warm and cozy, this comfortable feeling reminded her of her vacation.

Shuket's lips curved into a sweet smile, and she began to daydream again...

[P20] "During summer... I was playing windsurfing on a chestnut leaf... Hmm, this is so wonderful... the sun is caressing my back... but... but... but..."

[P21] But when Shuket still thought she was on the lake, her potion began to bubble up, producing many big bubbles!
A huge bubble quietly formed and rose from the small cauldron...
Suddenly, with a "pop," that bubble exploded!
Poor Shuket! She was covered head to toe in potion!

[P22] "You should turn the fire down a bit," Lucy laughed. "Goodness, how absent-minded you are!"

[P23] Magic School
The day is finally over!
After all the ups and downs of the day, Shuket is finally able to go home!

[P24] Just outside the school gate, Shuket saw little ladybug Zabel turning mushrooms into little hedgehogs!
"If you'd like," the ladybug said to Shuket, "I can teach you a magical dance, and you'll learn a fun trick..."

[P25] Shuket found a big mushroom as her target. This big mushroom was wearing a red hat, which reminded her of... Santa Claus!
Then, she fell into her fantasy again...

[P26] "Dear Santa Claus, the gifts I want this year are: a jar of gold powder to decorate my wings... a slug plush toy, some princess jewelry, and a few pieces of lettuce chocolate..."

[P27] Sukot was lost in her fantasy of countless gifts, jumping and jumping, completely forgetting everything around her.
As a result, the big mushroom didn't turn into a little hedgehog, but kept twisting and turning, as if someone was tickling it.
Then, something strange happened: the mushroom suddenly grew two legs and two big ears, and with a 'whoosh,' it bounced away, 'escaping'…

[P28] "How could this happen?!" Zabel exclaimed loudly, she could hardly believe her eyes, "Goodness, how absent-minded you are!"

[P29] The next morning, Schott made up her mind to stop daydreaming!
And today's outdoor activity class was super fun—she was going to learn how to shrink monsters.

[P30] Sukot was highly focused. She practiced on an old shoe and succeeded right away!
27

[P31] Suddenly, something terrifying happened: a terrible, gooey, crazy toad suddenly jumped out!
"How delicious! Yum yum, there are so many tasty snacks!" the crazy toad said, drooling, "Which one should I eat first?"

[P32] When everyone was shouting to run away, the slimy toad slowly approached Shuket...

[P33] Luckily, Shuket had memorized the magic spell this time. She hurriedly chanted:
"By the power of the big rat, turn this disgusting big monster into a tiny thing quickly!"

[P34] In the span of just one second, the slimy toad kept shrinking, shrinking, and shrinking again...
Until it became as small as a tiny flying insect.

[P35] "Well done, my little girl!" the spider teacher clapped, saying, "If it weren't for you, we might all have become the 'delicious meal' in the toad's stomach!"

[P36] "No matter what," Shuket said proudly, "one thing is certain: from now on, I'll never be distracted again!"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，展示了书名《心不住鸟的舒科特》及作者、绘者、译者信息，画面中央是戴着粉色眼镜的绿色毛毛虫舒科特，周围环绕着多个卡通昆虫角色，背景为星空和月亮。
[P2] 本页为绘本封面，展示书名《心不在焉的舒科特》及作者、绘者、译者信息，画面中央是戴着粉色眼镜的绿色毛毛虫舒科特，周围环绕着多个卡通昆虫角色，背景为星空和月亮。
[P3] 本页为绘本封面，展示书名《心不在焉的舒科特》及作者、绘者、译者信息，画面中央是戴着粉色眼镜的绿色毛毛虫舒科特，周围环绕着多个卡通昆虫角色，背景为星空和月亮。
[P4] 本页为出版者的话，阐述了情绪管理的重要性，强调幼儿时期是培养情绪管理能力的关键阶段，并介绍了该系列动物图画故事书的教育意义和亲子共读价值。
[P5] 本页为绘本的导读页，以‘老师对你说’为标题，介绍了故事《当幻想遇上心不在焉》的背景和主要内容，讲述了主角舒科特因幻想而心不在焉，后在紧急情况下凭借冷静和魔法解决问题的故事梗概。
[P6] 本页为一位幼儿园园长的推荐语，她以‘小毛毛虫舒科特’为例，阐述了孩子天性中的幻想与注意力并不矛盾，并建议家长理解、包容孩子，通过恰当方式培养其专注力，同时尊重其想象力，以促进孩子健康成长。
[P7] 本页描绘了小毛毛虫舒科特即将前往森林中央的老橡树洞魔法学校上学的场景，画面中巨大的橡树树洞上挂着‘魔法学校’的招牌，树洞内有一只戴眼镜的猫头鹰老师，周围环绕着秋叶和小动物，营造出开学的喜悦氛围。
[P8] 小毛毛虫舒科特在粉色的房间里兴奋地收拾新书包，准备上学，她把书包塞得满满的，并自言自语说东西都齐了。
[P9] 舒科特在去魔法学校上学的路上遇到拥挤，她利用自己的魔法能力变成蝴蝶，轻松地飞过人群。
[P10] 舒科特唱着魔法歌谣，成功变身为会飞的小蝴蝶，在蓝天中快乐飞翔，画面充满童趣与幻想色彩。
[P11] 舒科特在蓝天白云间飞翔，被微风吹拂，看着云朵开始幻想，画面充满童趣与梦幻氛围。
[P12] 小毛毛虫舒科特在蓝天中飞翔时，看着云朵展开想象，将云朵幻想成女巫、大熊和狼，表现出孩子丰富的想象力和对周围世界的奇妙联想。
[P13] 舒科特在空中飞翔时因胡思乱想撞上了一只大苍蝇，负责交通的雄蜂赶来责备她心不在焉。
[P14] 舒科特因撞上大苍蝇而感到羞愧，她加快速度，急匆匆地飞往学校所在的老橡树。
[P15] 舒科特在进入教室前变回毛毛虫形态，怯生生地敲响了树洞教室的门。
[P16] 舒科特进入魔法学校教室后，蜘蛛老师因她迟到而不满，让她坐在前排树根上，并要求她拿出小坩埚，准备配制能改变花朵颜色的药水。
[P17] 小萤火虫露西正在指导舒科特如何配制能改变花朵颜色的药水，她详细说明了步骤，包括用羊齿草的梗搅拌，待药水变白后再加入一小片彩虹。
[P18] 舒科特在配制药水时，眼镜被蒸汽模糊，她努力集中注意力完成任务。
[P19] 阳光照进教室，舒科特感到温暖舒适，回忆起假期，嘴角微笑，又开始幻想。
[P20] 舒科特在阳光下回忆夏天的美好时光，想象自己在栗树叶上玩帆板，但思绪突然中断，陷入犹豫和不确定中。
[P21] 舒科特在配制药水时，因分心幻想而使药水翻腾，一个大泡泡形成后爆炸，导致她全身沾满药水。
[P22] 舒科特在配制药水时因分心导致药水翻腾并爆炸，露西看到后笑着提醒她应该把火关小一点，并责备她心不在焉。
[P23] 一天的魔法学校课程结束，舒科特在同学们的陪伴下准备回家，画面展现了学校门口热闹的场景。
[P24] 舒科特刚走出魔法学校，遇到小瓢虫扎贝尔正在用魔法把蘑菇变成小刺猬，扎贝尔主动提出教她一种神奇的魔法舞蹈。
[P25] 舒科特将一朵戴红帽子的大蘑菇当作目标，联想到圣诞老人，随即又陷入幻想中。
[P26] 舒科特在幻想中写下给圣诞老人的礼物清单，包括金粉、鼻涕虫毛绒玩具、公主首饰和莴苣巧克力，画面中她戴着粉色眼镜，周围浮现着这些礼物的想象图。
[P27] 舒科特沉浸在幻想中，导致她用魔法变出的蘑菇没有变成刺猬，反而长出腿和耳朵，蹦跳着逃跑了。
[P28] 扎贝儿看到舒科特用魔法变出的蘑菇长出腿和耳朵后逃跑，惊讶地感叹她太心不在焉了。
[P29] 第二天早晨，舒科特决心不再做白日梦，并期待即将开始的室外活动课，学习如何把怪物变小。
[P30] 舒科特专注地练习魔法，成功将一只旧鞋子变成了目标物体，展现了她集中注意力后的成果。
[P31] 一只黏糊糊的癫蛤蟆突然出现，流着口水，兴奋地感叹眼前有太多可口的点心，不知该先吃哪一个。
[P32] 画面中，一只黏糊糊的癫蛤蟆正缓缓逼近舒科特，而扎贝尔在空中飞舞，舒科特则显得有些惊慌，背景是户外的草地和蒲公英。
[P33] 舒科特面对逼近的黏糊糊癫蛤蟆，回忆起魔法口诀并念出咒语，试图将其变小。
[P34] 舒科特成功念出咒语，将逼近的黏糊糊癫蛤蟆瞬间缩小至与小飞虫一般大小。
[P35] 蜘蛛老师表扬舒科特成功将癫蛤蟆变小，称赞她拯救了大家，避免了被吃掉的危险。
[P36] 舒科特在成功使用魔法后，自豪地表示自己再也不会心不在焉了。
[P37] 画面中，扎贝尔化身为一只绿色的小蝴蝶，在蓝天白云间快乐地飞翔，翅膀为粉红色，带有绿色斑点，周围点缀着星星和飘动的丝带，展现出轻松愉悦的氛围。
